method_survey.oss_survey: pylbm (~/oss-cache/pylbm/pylbm/analysis/stability.py): symbolic amplification matrix via sympy, eigenvalue computation, Cohn-Schur stability test; Maarten-vd-Sande/lbm: no explicit stability analysis module
key_findings: Von Neumann stability analysis for LBM is a well-established technique (Sterling & Chen 1996, Lallemand & Luo 2000)
The amplification matrix A(theta) = diag(exp(-i theta.c_i)) P where P is the linearized collision operator
Eigenvalues mu give per-timestep amplification; stable iff max|mu| <= 1
Mode identification requires overlap with k->0 eigendirections (shear: transverse velocity; sound: density)
TensorLBM already has a complete implementation in src/tensorlbm/stability/von_neumann.py with 27 tests
The missing piece was an automated cross-validation benchmark packaging the analysis
method_survey.selected_approach: Build on existing tensorlbm.stability.von_neumann module; create automated benchmark (run_xval.py) that runs both analytic and measured arms, compares point-by-point, and generates result.json with all numbers programmatically
method_survey.rationale: Leverage existing, tested implementation; add automated cross-validation pipeline following the Chapman-Enskog AUTO pattern
